**Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Subject: Religious Studies (code 0785), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2022. Paper 2: The Old Testament/Jewish Bible and World Faiths. Duration: three hours.**

Instructions to candidates: Answer FOUR questions chosen from any ONE SECTION ONLY. All questions carry equal marks (25 marks each).

You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.

Sections of the paper: 1.0 The Old Testament/Jewish Bible, Section 1.1 The Patriarchs to David (questions 1 to 6); Section 5.3 Islam (questions 7 to 12); Section 5.5 African Traditional Religious Beliefs and Practices (questions 13 to 18).

À faire relire par un spécialiste des études religieuses avant mise en avant.

questions.enonce_markdown: Obedience to Allah and His Messenger is an obligation in Islam. Assess the validity of this statement. (25 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Introduction.** Islam means submission to God. Muslims believe that submission is shown by obeying God and the messenger He sent, Muhammad. The statement claims that this obedience is an obligation. This answer assesses its validity.

**1. Evidence that the statement is valid.**
- *The Qur'an commands it.* The Qur'an repeatedly says "Obey God and obey the Messenger", and it tells the believers that whoever obeys the Messenger has obeyed God. It also says that believers have no choice in a matter once God and His Messenger have decided it.
- *The declaration of faith.* The shahada joins the two: "There is no god but God, and Muhammad is the Messenger of God". To become a Muslim one has to accept both the authority of God and the role of the Messenger.
- *The Messenger as model.* The Qur'an presents the Prophet as an excellent example to follow. His words, actions and approvals (the Sunnah, preserved in the hadith) explain how to carry out the commands of the Qur'an: for example, the details of prayer, zakat, fasting and pilgrimage are known mainly from his practice.
- *The Sunnah as a source of law.* Among the sources of Islamic law the Qur'an comes first and the Sunnah second, so obedience to the Messenger has legal force.
- *Examples in early Muslim history.* The companions obeyed the Prophet in matters of worship, war and daily life, as in the treaty of Hudaybiyyah, accepted by the Muslims despite their doubts. The Prophet is said to have promised that obedience to him leads to paradise.
- *A condition of faith.* Muslims hold that faith is not complete without accepting the Prophet's judgments willingly.

**2. Points that qualify the statement.**
- Obedience to the Messenger is a part of obedience to God and not separate from it, because the Prophet only conveyed the revelation. Obedience is not to Muhammad as a person with his own authority.
- The Qur'an also commands obedience to "those in authority" among the believers, but a saying of the Prophet states that there is no obedience to any creature in disobedience of the Creator. Obedience is therefore not blind.
- Muslims differ about the authenticity and interpretation of some hadith, and about how to apply the Sunnah to new situations (ijtihad). A small group of Muslims (sometimes called Quranists) accepts the Qur'an as the only source, but this is a minority view.
- Obedience is meant to come from love and conviction, not only fear, and the Qur'an says there is no compulsion in religion.

**3. Assessment.** The statement is well supported by the Qur'an and by the Sunnah, and by the beliefs of the main Muslim traditions (Sunni and Shi'a, who differ on other questions of authority after the Prophet). It is a basic principle of Muslim faith and practice.

**Conclusion.** The statement is valid: obedience to Allah and His Messenger is an obligation in Islam, with the qualification that obedience to the Messenger is part of obedience to God and is practised through understanding, not in contradiction to the Qur'an.
